_decision: WITHDRAWN, 2026-09-05. This project does not quote a false-positive rate, a recall figure, or any aggregate detection metric. Every gate below is null. The corpus eval is a RATCHET, not a measurement: eval/baseline.json records a per-case prediction and the run fails when a case that was right becomes wrong. That question needs no statistical validity, because it compares a run against the previous run rather than against a claim about the world.
_why: The gates were set at 0.3 FPR against a stated target of 0.02 - deliberately, so the run would not sit permanently red. That gap was the tell. A gate nobody expects to bind is not a standard, and the longer it sat in the repo the likelier one of its numbers ended up quoted somewhere it could not be supported. Maintaining thresholds that cannot bear weight is worse than having none.
_the_arithmetic: What settled it was working out what would actually breach each gate at the corpus sizes we have. GB is gated at 0.85 recall on TWO scam cases; US and NZ on one each; IE on zero, so its recall gate is unreachable by construction. One missed case breaches GB, US and NZ. Those gates were therefore already ratchets - 'never regress on this one case' - wearing a percentage that implied a population estimate. baseline.json does that job properly and names the case that flipped. Only AU (26 scam / 30 benign) has enough cases for a gate to mean anything, and 3 misses would breach it. One region's coarse gate is not worth the misreading the other five invite.
_what_replaces_it: Three things, none of which needs a labelled population estimate. (1) baseline.json - per-case ratchet, fails on any correct-to-incorrect flip. (2) The metamorphic harness - consistency relations that need no labels at all, so they scale to regions we have no corpus for. (3) The region relations - invariance and coverage-monotonicity, which catch pack leakage the corpus cannot see.
_what_would_reopen_this: A corpus with enough labelled cases per slice to distinguish the numbers being gated. That means mechanical stratified sampling from reports plus blind labelling - roughly a day of work that no tooling removes - and it is currently blocked upstream: submission volume is too low to stratify. Item 1 in the roadmap establishes that. If that changes, the honest move is to re-derive gates from the new corpus rather than to un-null these.
_reading_a_run: The printed tables still show recall, FPR and confidence intervals per slice. They are diagnostics for whoever is looking at a change, not standards, and the intervals beside them are the reason: a slice reading 100.0% [21-100] is telling you it knows almost nothing. Read the interval before the number, and do not carry either into a claim.
